column2: *** 1845, June quarter, THE HOLBORN UNION - Volume 02, page 149 ***
column4: *** THE SPELLING CONTROL AND A REAL FIND AT ONCE. *** The query said BRAYLEY and the index returned BRAILEY, which is what makes the nulls below trustworthy. *** AND HE SETTLES THREE THINGS. *** (1) *** THE TREE'S 22 JUNE 1845 IS RIGHT *** - a June birth falls in the June quarter - and the 1900 death index, which gave his age as 53 and implied 1847, had a careless informant, exactly as this archive concluded from the 1851 census. (2) *** THE BIRTHPLACE DISPUTE RESOLVES TO NEITHER SIDE: *** the census says ST PANCRAS and the tree says ST PAUL'S, and the registration district is *** HOLBORN *** - which is where his sister ISABELLA was born, recorded in 1861 as "London (City), ST ANDREW", that is St Andrew Holborn. (3) *** HIS MIDDLE NAME IS WALKER. ***

column2: *** 1850, September quarter, THE BIDEFORD UNION - Volume 10, page 52 ***
column4: *** CONFIRMS A CORRECTION THIS ARCHIVE MADE FROM A CENSUS. *** The tree said "b. 1851, Bideford"; the 1851 census showed her eight months old on 30 March 1851 and data/1851-bideford-brayley.tsv called the tree *** a year late ***. A September-quarter 1850 registration is exactly that.

column1: *** AND THE TWO WHO ARE NOT THERE ***
column4: *** ISABELLA BRAILEY, born about 1841 at St Andrew, London, and MARY ANN HELLEN BRAYLEY, born 20 May 1843 at St Bartholomew's, City of London. *** Neither has a birth registration under this mother, in any spelling the index will reach, across fifteen years. *** THE NULL IS NOW DOUBLE AND IT COMES FROM TWO DIRECTIONS: *** FreeBMD could not find Mary Ann Hellen under her own name in September, and the GRO cannot find her under her mother's in October.

column1: # ============ *** WHAT THE PATTERN SAYS, AND IT DATES ITSELF ============ ***
# *** THE TWO EARLIEST CHILDREN ARE UNREGISTERED AND THE TWO LATER ONES ARE REGISTERED. ***
#   Isabella, about 1841, London - NOT REGISTERED
#   Mary Ann Hellen, 20 May 1843, City of London - NOT REGISTERED
#   John Walker, June 1845, Holborn - REGISTERED
#   Georgina Margaret, September 1850, Bideford - REGISTERED
# *** REGISTRATION WAS NOT COMPULSORY ON PARENTS UNTIL THE BIRTHS AND DEATHS REGISTRATION ACT 1874,
# IN FORCE FROM 1875. *** Before that the duty lay on the registrar, and under-registration in the
# 1840s is well attested and concentrated among the urban poor. *** THIS FAMILY IS DESCRIBED IN THE
# 1851 CENSUS AS "SHOEMAKER WIFE PAUPER". ***
# *** SO THE HONEST READING: Mary Ann Hellen was almost certainly never registered, and the archive
# should stop looking for her birth entry. *** That is a conclusion and not a certainty - a
# registration under a wholly unrelated spelling, or in a surname the index does not associate with
# BRAYLEY at all, cannot be excluded by any search.
